+;.
+define weak void @__omp_offloading_2c_38c77_sequential_loop_l4() #0 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define {{[^@]+}}@__omp_offloading_2c_38c77_sequential_loop_l4
+; CHECK-SAME: () #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[DOTZERO_ADDR:%.*]] = alloca i32, align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[DOTTHREADID_TEMP_:%.*]] = alloca i32, align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 0, i32* [[DOTZERO_ADDR]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = call i32 @__kmpc_target_init(%struct.ident_t* @[[GLOB1]], i1 true, i1 false, i1 true)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXEC_USER_CODE:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[TMP0]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXEC_USER_CODE]], label [[USER_CODE_ENTRY:%.*]], label [[WORKER_EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       user_code.entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = call i32 @__kmpc_global_thread_num(%struct.ident_t* @[[GLOB1]]) #[[ATTR2:[0-9]+]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[TMP1]], i32* [[DOTTHREADID_TEMP_]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @__omp_outlined__(i32* noalias nocapture noundef nonnull readonly align 4 dereferenceable(4) [[DOTTHREADID_TEMP_]], i32* noalias nocapture noundef nonnull readnone align 4 dereferenceable(4) [[DOTZERO_ADDR]]) #[[ATTR2]]

top_candidates.subject: [DivRemPairs] Add an initial case for hoisting to a common predecessor.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends the DivRemPairs scalar optimization with a common-predecessor hoisting case. When a remainder block uniquely flows into a division block and all predecessor successors are either of those blocks, optimizeDivRem moves the division, and for native div-rem operations the remainder as well, before the predecessor terminator; otherwise it retains the prior behavior of declining the transformation. The accompanying test expectation updates require the division to appear earlier and, for i128, expect the remainder to be decomposed into multiply/subtract using frozen operands.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; remainder_triangle_i64 test checks; remainder_triangle_i128 test checks
Behavioral change: Adds a new CFG-sensitive transformation that hoists matching division/remainder operations to a common predecessor block.; Uses IsSafeToHoist to require instructions preceding the moved div/rem in their original blocks to be guaranteed to transfer execution to a successor.; Requires RemBB to have DivBB as its single successor, RemBB to have a unique predecessor, and every predecessor successor to be either RemBB or DivBB.; Sets DivDominates after hoisting the division; when there is a native div-rem operation, it also hoists the remainder, otherwise subsequent logic can rewrite the remainder as multiply/subtract.
Assertion or trace link: DivDominates; common-predecessor hoisting; Instruction::moveBefore
Reproducer link: The updated remainder_triangle_i64 and remainder_triangle_i128 checks cover the new triangular CFG hoisting behavior, but the retrieved evidence does not establish that PR50585's compact C reproducer reaches DivRemPairs.; The i128 expectation changes show the transformation can combine hoisting with freeze insertion and remainder decomposition, increasing the verifier-sensitive value-placement surface.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Transforms/Scalar/DivRemPairs; DominatorTree-aware scalar optimizer transformation
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it newly relocates IR instructions across basic blocks and explicitly reasons about whether the division dominates the remainder. Such movement can directly cause the reported verifier class of failure if an instruction is placed before one of its required definitions or a moved value is used along a path it no longer dominates. The shown safety predicate establishes guaranteed control transfer before the operations and constrains CFG shape, but the retrieved hunk does not itself show a corresponding operand-dominance check at the new insertion point. That is evidence of a plausible mechanism, though not proof that the PR50585 testcase invokes this pass or this exact case.
Causal confidence: 0.68

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes Mach-O linker lazy-binding setup to create dyld_stub_binder through the normal undefined-symbol path rather than looking it up directly. StubHelperSection::setup now calls SymbolTable::addUndefined, processes a remaining Undefined through treatUndefinedSymbol, then rechecks whether resolution replaced the symbol with a DylibSymbol before using it as the stub binder.
Changed symbols: StubHelperSection::setup
Behavioral change: dyld_stub_binder is now registered as an undefined symbol through symtab->addUndefined instead of being obtained with symtab->find.; Undefined-symbol diagnostics and resolution are delegated to treatUndefinedSymbol for lazy binding.; The code accounts for treatUndefinedSymbol changing the symbol representation by recasting binder to DylibSymbol before adding it to the GOT.
Reproducer link: No retrieved first-parent hunk concerns Clang -O1 optimization, LLVM IR construction, or an invalid-IR verifier failure.
Pass or subsystem link: lld Mach-O synthetic-section and symbol-resolution machinery
Causal explanation: The candidate changes linker-side Mach-O undefined-symbol handling after compilation, not an LLVM scalar optimization or IR/CFG/value-replacement utility.
